head: 75683bfbd195afd7d12b45c8a55f359c44eaca0e
why: Today's CI tooling, tracker 1144. The plan says to revise before rollout if the measured overhead is material. P9's fixture pairs compare against a tiny run, about 0.55 s, so its fixed startup cost reads as about 110%. This row measures the same reporter on real tests, so the lead can make that call against a real run's length. Lead's call: about 3% wall on real tests, legs well under their 17-minute limit (0598's runs: 6.8 to 11.7 min), so the rollout goes ahead. Making the append and startup faster is a follow-up ticket, not this pull request. About 75% sure. The doubt is a next/ leg whose tests are denser in callbacks than these. What settles it is the first scheduled full run's test-step times after merge, compared with the runs before it. The timing artifact already records them.
note: Cloud box, Node 26.13.0, nice 15, `--maxWorkers=3`, the same 30 tooling test files each time (15 from oxlint-plugins/, 15 from .github/ci/workflow-lint/, no integration file), 658 tests, all passed every run. Each pair ran the baseline first, then the reporter. Both used `--reporter=default --reporter=json`, and the second also used `--reporter=./.github/ci/progress-reporter.ts`, with RUNNER_TEMP and a fixed fixture identity set so it really wrote. Wall ms, baseline then reporter: 186460 / 188344, 186266 / 191810, 186669 / 195857. Extra: 1884, 5544, 9188 ms, mean 5539 ms, 3.0% (1.0% to 4.9%). Vitest's own Duration agrees: 185.14 / 186.99, 185.13 / 190.60, 185.51 / 194.58 s. Each reporter journal held 1446 records, 219712 bytes. That is about 3.8 ms of wall per record on a shared, niced box. The extra grew from pair to pair, and three pairs cannot say whether that is drift or noise. No change to the source. Raw logs stay in the session's scratch, not in git.
